newsitem.title: SPAIN: Mexican ex-prosecutor held by Spanish police.
newsitem.headline: Mexican ex-prosecutor held by Spanish police.

text.p: A former Mexican prosecutor who had the ex-president's brother jailed on murder charges was in Spanish police custody on Saturday facing possible extradition, officials said.
Pablo Chapa Bezanilla was prosecutor in the case of Raul Salinas, imprisoned since 1995 on charges of murder and illicit enrichment and brother to former president Carlos Salinas.
Chapa, who turned fugitive after Mexican authorities accused him of evidence-tampering and body snatching, was arrested on Friday night in Madrid, Spanish government officials said.
He was expected to appear before a Spanish judge as early as Monday to determine whether he should be held for extradition to Mexico, they said.

The charges against Chapa arose from the discovery of a human skeleton in late 1996 at the Mexico City ranch of Raul Salinas. Chapa oversaw the excavation of the bones and suggested they were those of a missing congressman who was wanted on charges of helping Salinas to plan a political killing. Salinas denies involvement in the murder.

But authorities later determined that the skeleton belonged to a relative of a psychic who was helping Chapa with the investigation. Officials said it was dug up from a cemetery and planted at the ranch.
Chapa was fired from the attorney general's office in December 1996 and has been in hiding since February.
An international arrest warrant issued by the Mexican government accused Chapa of providing false information, violating burial laws and illegal using his powers as a government official.
